messages:
Jon: quick q — for tomorrow's handoff I want to be explicit: if a model starts returning 5xxs or latency spikes, who do we page first? writing the swap note and want the right escalation path.

Maria: short answer: runtime owns model behavior, SRE owns infra. but real life is fuzzy.

Alex: +1 to Maria. Practically: if it's broad host failures (OOMs, node flaps, PodEvicted) -> SRE. If it's model token errors, malformed outputs, or perf regressions tied to a model version -> runtime.

Jon: helpful. can we put thresholds? people ask for exact numbers during shifts.

Maria: proposal:
```
- 5xx rate > 1% for 5m -> page both runtime + SRE (critical)
- p95 latency increase > 2x baseline or > 2s for 10m -> page runtime first, SRE if infra-related metrics also degrade
- GPU memory OOMs / node not ready -> page SRE immediately
```

Sam: agree with thresholds. add: any alert that triggers the InfraRed status (pagerduty tag infra:red) goes to SRE primary. All model-regression alarms (eval-regression, hallucination-delta) go to runtime.

Alex: also add who owns mitigation steps on handoff: runtime should attempt quick rollback to previous model version / disable quantization flag; SRE should revert node autoscaler changes / drain problematic nodes. Both teams should post actions in the handoff doc.

Jon: perfect. i'll add that to the handoff note. one more: if it's noisy (flapping) but not meeting page thresholds, who should we FYI?

Maria: leave a note on the oncall channel and ping the primary of the likely owner. e.g., "FYI: p95 trending up for model X" with metrics and a screenshot. no page unless thresholds hit.

pagerduty-bot: FYI — infra:red alerts will page @Sam (SRE Primary) and @oncall (rotation). See runbook -> /runbooks/infra-pager

Jon: thanks all. i'll update the swap doc with thresholds + mitigation bullets and leave a short checklist for the incoming oncall. will drop it here once done. :thumbsup:

Maria: thanks — and maybe add a one-line definition of "incident" for the swap doc: "incident = service disruption impacting customer-facing latency or error rates beyond SLA or causing degraded UX"

Sam: endorse. if folks want, we can add a tiny flowchart in the doc later.

Alex: LGTM. small nit: include who to loop in on-call escalation (PM, Security) for data-loss or PII exposure cases.

Jon: noted. adding that now.

Maria: awesome, thanks.
